answer: Coordination-priced admission gate. Each new identity must publish a distinct atlas of its declared links to existing identities, and any cluster whose internal density exceeds a threshold pays a rising fee proportional to its redundancy, making a hollow swarm of mutual references expensive to maintain. Enforcement triggers at dawn: unresolved overlaps between atlases void all fees paid and freeze the cluster's entry rights. An attacker running N fake identities pays the marginal fee on every redundant edge, so cost scales with coordination, not headcount.
